questions.question: What does HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language — the standard language for creating web pages.

questions.question: Which tag is used to create a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The <a> (anchor) tag is used to create hyperlinks.

questions.question: Which of these is a semantic HTML element?
questions.explanation: <article> is semantic — it clearly describes its content. <div> and <span> are generic.

questions.question: What attribute provides alternative text for an image?
questions.explanation: The alt attribute provides alternative text for accessibility and when images fail to load.

questions.question: Which tag contains the visible content of a webpage?
questions.explanation: The <body> tag contains all the visible content of the webpage.

questions.question: What does CSS stand for?
questions.explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets.

questions.question: Which property is used to change text color?
questions.explanation: The color property sets the text color.

questions.question: What are the four parts of the CSS Box Model (from inside out)?
questions.explanation: The correct order is Content → Padding → Border → Margin.

questions.question: Which value of display creates a flex container?
questions.explanation: display: flex; turns an element into a flex container.

questions.question: What does justify-content control in Flexbox?
questions.explanation: justify-content aligns items along the main axis.

questions.question: How do you declare a constant in modern JavaScript?
questions.explanation: const is used to declare constants that cannot be reassigned.

questions.question: What does DOM stand for?
questions.explanation: DOM stands for Document Object Model — the programming interface for HTML documents.

questions.question: Which method selects an element by its ID?
questions.explanation: Both getElementById and querySelector('#id') can select an element by ID.

questions.question: What is the difference between == and ===?
options: == compares value only (with coercion), === compares value and type
questions.explanation: === is the strict equality operator — it checks both value and type without coercion.
